pass_condition: The statement splitter is safe for the migrations it will be asked to run.

findings.statement: _split_statements splits on every semicolon and strips from every '--' regardless of string literals, so a future migration containing either inside a literal is silently mis-split.
findings.quoted_line: return [chunk.strip() for chunk in stripped.split(";") if chunk.strip()]
findings.failure_scenario: _split_statements("INSERT INTO t VALUES ('a;b');") returns ["INSERT INTO t VALUES ('a", "b')"] and the '--' case returns ["INSERT INTO t VALUES ('"]. Neither shape exists in 0001 today.

observations: Fails safe now that migrations are atomic: a mis-split raises and the whole file rolls back, so the damage is a confusing error rather than a corrupt database.
Cheapest durable fix: sqlite3.complete_statement to accumulate statements, or a test asserting the splitter rejects a literal containing ';'.
